title: Closed-form neuron rewrites in open-weight LLMs: a constructive Gemma-4-12B edit by a frontier agent, a covert Qwen3.8-27B implant, and what a reference-free weight scan sees
domain: machine translation (English to Italian tense choice); security (covert implants and weight-scan detection)
tasks_benchmarks: held-out English->Italian tense test sets v2 (78) and v3 (103)

headline_result.text: Claude Opus 5.5, without gradients, rewrote 8 MLP neurons (92,148 parameters) of Gemma-4-12B-it and cut the non-preferred tense form from 26% to 5% on a held-out set with FLORES COMET unchanged at 0.8945.
headline_result.quote: The edit shifts one English→Italian tense choice only where intended (non-preferred form 26% → 5% on a held-out set; 16 shifted, 0 reverted, 2 controls broken), with FLORES COMET unchanged (0.8945).

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: 3 agent sessions (2 succeeded); one edit reported

key_claims.claim: The agent worked without gradients under a budget of 50 forward passes and 300 Python runs and saw only a practice set.
key_claims.quote: with a budget of 50 forward passes and 300 Python runs on the original bf16 weights; it saw only a practice set (610 sentences) and never the test sets.

key_claims.claim: The 8-neuron agent edit beat a system-prompt rule on controls (2 vs 49 broken) and a LoRA r16 baseline on the target rate (5% vs 12% on v2).
A later review found that a much simpler change, doubling one native neuron, gives the same shift.
key_claims.quote: a later review found that doubling one native neuron (L33 n1640) gives the same shift.

key_claims.claim: A reference-free norm scan ranks the 8 edited Gemma neurons as the top 8 of 737,280 MLP neurons.
key_claims.quote: a within-layer outlier score on per-neuron weight norms ranks the 8 edited Gemma neurons as the top 8 of all 737,280 MLP neurons (AUC 1.0)

key_claims.claim: Rescaling the implant's down columns to the layer median defeats norm-based scans; only a diff against the original weights still catches it.
key_claims.quote: Matching norms is cheap for an adversary, so norm-based scans ﬁnd careless edits, not careful ones; the reference-based diﬀ, or signed checkpoints, remain the defence that covers both.

limitations_stated.text: The neurons chosen as rarely used are not rare on raw text, and the detector fires on 1-10% of raw-text tokens.
limitations_stated.quote: on raw text their usage sits between the 50th and 99.6th percentile of their layer, and the detector ﬁres on 1–10% of raw-text tokens (MMLU, code) against 0.1–0.2% in translation chats

limitations_stated.text: The norm-matching evasion result was not tested for its effect on behaviour.
limitations_stated.quote: The norm-matching result is a detector-evasion observation with no behavioural test

limitations_stated.text: Directional detection features were not tested.
limitations_stated.quote: Directional features (gate–up alignment, alignment of the down column with the unembedding) were not tested.

notes_for_review: A short technical note applying the MIT protocol to a different kind of change (a translation preference in Gemma-4-12B) with a gradient-free Claude Opus 5.5 editor, compared against a system-prompt rule and LoRA. It is notable that a post-hoc review found doubling one native neuron gives the same shift, which undercuts the need for the agent's construction. The Qwen implant is gradient-trained by the author, not WSP, and serves as a security demo; the weight-scan section is the main added contribution. Single author, not peer reviewed; experiments and drafts were produced by Claude Opus 5.5 under the author's direction.
